module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 79

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/79](https://www.erdosproblems.com/79)
- [EFRS93] Erdős, P., Faudree, R. J., Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., Ramsey size linear graphs.
  Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 389-399.
- [Wi24] Wigderson, Y., Infinitely many minimally non-Ramsey size linear graphs.
  arXiv:2409.05931 (2024).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos79

open scoped Classical in
/--
We say $G$ is Ramsey size linear if $R(G,H)\ll m$ for all graphs $H$ with $m$ edges and
no isolated vertices.

Are there infinitely many graphs $G$ which are not Ramsey size linear but such that all of
its proper subgraphs are?

Asked by Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [EFRS93]. $K_4$ was long the only known example.
Wigderson [Wi24] proved that there are infinitely many such graphs.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_79 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : N ≤ n) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      ¬ G.IsRamseySizeLinear ∧
      ∀ H : G.Subgraph, H < ⊤ → H.coe.IsRamseySizeLinear := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos79

reformulations.difference: The source asks for infinitely many minimally non-Ramsey-size-linear graphs. Lean expresses this as the existence of such a graph on Fin n with n ≥ N for every natural number N.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite simple graph has a representative on Fin n. There are only finitely many graphs on each Fin n, hence finitely many isomorphism classes of bounded order; conversely, isomorphic graphs have the same order. Thus infinitely many isomorphism classes is equivalent to unbounded vertex counts. The exact equivalence for the theorem's graph predicate was proved as Review79.erdos79_infinitely_many_isoClasses_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the reviewed theorem or sorry-dependent results.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/79 — statement, affirmative solved status, and remarks; read through https://r.jina.ai/http://www.erdosproblems.com/79 because direct requests returned a Cloudflare challenge.

Yuval Wigderson, Infinitely many minimally non-Ramsey size-linear graphs, arXiv:2409.05931v2: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05931 and full LaTeX source from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2409.05931. Read the definition, Theorem 1, its proof, and the concluding question about explicit examples.

Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, Ramsey Size Linear Graphs, Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 2 (1993), 389–399, DOI 10.1017/S096354830000078X. Read the publisher's abstract and bibliographic information at https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S096354830000078X/type/journal_article; full text was unavailable.

Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/{Basic,Copy,Subgraph,Finite}.lean; Mathlib/Data/Set/Card.lean; Mathlib/Order/Lattice/Nat.lean — graph containment, subgraph order and coercion, degrees, edge cardinalities, and natural-number infima.
review.notes: The sole theorem matches Wigderson's Theorem 1, and both answer(True) and research solved agree with the problem page. Checked that graphRamsey uses non-induced copies and the vertex Ramsey number, that the linearity constant is uniform over all opponents, and that H < ⊤ ranges over proper subgraphs with H.coe on their actual vertex sets. Boundary experiments verified degree/edge-count conventions and proved that an empty opponent has Ramsey number zero and that every edgeless candidate is Ramsey size linear. The scratch file compiles successfully; its equivalence and boundary proofs have no sorryAx dependency. Although the original 1993 full text could not be retrieved, the cited Wigderson paper explicitly supplies the original question, definition, and affirmative solution, so the declaration's faithfulness is settled.
